title: Robot Explorers
objective: After this level you can describe how robotic probes like Voyager explored the outer planets.
summary: The twin Voyagers (1977) toured the giant planets; Voyager 2 alone visited Uranus and Neptune; Voyager 1 is now interstellar.

cards.headline: The farthest thing humans ever built is still sending messages home.
The grand tour
cards.body: Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 launched in 1977. Between them they flew past Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. Voyager 2 is still the only spacecraft to have visited Uranus, in 1986, and Neptune, in 1989.

cards.headline: Into interstellar space
cards.body: In 2012 Voyager 1 crossed into interstellar space, the most distant human-made object. Each Voyager carries a Golden Record of sounds and images from Earth, a message for anyone who might one day find it.

cards.fact: Voyager 1’s radio signals take more than 20 hours to reach Earth.
cards.context: Traveling at the speed of light, each message from the edge of the solar system is almost a day old when it arrives, and the gap grows every year.

cards.headline: Robot explorers: logged
learned: They flew past all four giant planets
Voyager 2 alone visited Uranus and Neptune

questions.prompt: Which spacecraft is the only one to have visited Uranus and Neptune?

options.label: Voyager 1
options.rationale: Voyager 1 left the planets after Saturn.

options.label: The James Webb telescope
options.rationale: Webb orbits far from the giant planets.

questions.explanation: Voyager 2 flew past Uranus in 1986 and Neptune in 1989, the only spacecraft ever to visit them.

questions.prompt: What is special about Voyager 1’s location today?

options.label: It has reached interstellar space, farther than any human-made object
It is orbiting Neptune’s largest moon
It has landed on the surface of Pluto
options.rationale: No spacecraft has landed on Pluto.

options.label: It has returned to orbit around the Earth

questions.explanation: Voyager 1 entered interstellar space in 2012 and is the most distant object humans have made.

questions.prompt: From Level 29: Herschel found Uranus with a telescope in 1781. How did Voyager 2 add to that?

options.label: It discovered Uranus a second time
It gave humanity its only close-up visit to Uranus
It brought rock samples back from Uranus
options.rationale: No mission has returned samples from Uranus.

options.label: It landed on the surface of Uranus
options.rationale: Uranus has no solid surface to land on.

questions.explanation: Herschel spotted Uranus from Earth; Voyager 2’s 1986 flyby remains the only close-up visit.
